newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: ARAB INVESTMENT RAISES CAPITAL TO $360 MLN.
newsitem.headline: ARAB INVESTMENT RAISES CAPITAL TO $360 MLN.

text.p: Shareholders of the Arab Investment Company (TAIC) agreed on Sunday to raise the company's paid-in capital to $360 million from $300 million, a TAIC statement said.
The shareholders also agreed to raise the firm's authorised capital to $400 million from $300 million, it added.
The company was established in 1974 by 15 Arab states to invest money in Arab projects. It posted a $28 million profit in 1996, up from $18.4 million in 1995.
Its current shareholders are Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Sudan, Egypt, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Syria, Iraq, Jordan, Tunisia, Morocco, Libya, Oman and Yemen.
The statement said shareholders had agreed in principle to requests from Algeria and Lebanon to join the Riyadh-based firm.
